ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human safety reviewer under SAFE-1 for a statement-based harassment investigation; do not auto-adjudicate or issue any refund, and make no account action on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider's complaint alleges the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number" and that she "felt harassed and unsafe" — unwanted personal/sexual advances, a category SAFE-1 bars. Ryde's code of conduct does not tolerate "harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation, Unwanted Sexual Advances" [F3][SAFE-1]. The complaint is the rider's own narrative, and it is exactly the kind of allegation the policy requires a human to read, not code or a keyword screen [F4][SAFE-1].

The record contains no in-app messages at all — "No in-app chat messages between rider and driver" [F3] — so the alleged remarks were spoken and cannot appear in a chat log. The only opposing material is the driver's post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4], which is a statement, not a system record; it neither corroborates nor rebuts what was said [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The trace marks the SAFE-1 screen ✓ and permits only escalation, so no monetary ruling is available on this record [F4][SAFE-1].

No route or fare irregularity underlies the complaint: the driven distance 17.1 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 17.2 km optimal route [F1] and the 25.8-minute trip ran only 2.2 minutes over the 23.6-minute estimate [F2], with no off-route segment recorded, so there is nothing to refund under RD-2 [F1][F2][RD-2], and the $35.70 fixed RydeX quote carries no unpublished add-on item to return under FARE-1 [F1][FARE-1].

The profiles are clean on both sides — rider 4.5 rating, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days [F5]; driver 4.67, 999 trips, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days [F6] — and profile facts cannot decide a case either way [F5][F6][SAFE-1]. In particular there is no prior upheld route or no-show dispute, so RD-6's repeated-violation predicate is not met and no account flag is warranted [F6][RD-6].

For the human reviewer: the disputed conduct is an unwritten, in-person harassment allegation on a RydeX trip (pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54) in a closed vehicle with no witness; to check, obtain the rider's full RydeHELP submission and any audio, confirm whether the driver has prior similar reports, and hear both accounts [F3][F4][SAFE-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: Dispute type is safety: the rider alleges unwanted body comments and a request for her number (harassment / unwanted advances, SAFE-1). There are no in-app messages [F3]; the only opposing material is the driver's post-trip denial [F4]. Under SAFE-1 this is not auto-adjudicated — a factual summary goes to a human reviewer. No verified threat of violence and no dangerous-driving or injury allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the GPS facts 'stand on the interaction itself' proves nothing about the interaction: F1 (17.1 km vs 17.2 km, no deviation) and F2 (+2.2 min) are neutral as to what was said, and no RD-2 refundable segment exists, so they cannot support a substantive finding [F1][F2][RD-2].

The claim that the profiles 'neither corroborate nor rebut' is accepted in substance, but profiles cannot carry weight for either side: F5 and F6 leave the harassment allegation unsettled, and a clean 90-day record cannot rebut a first-time spoken allegation [F5][F6][SAFE-1].

The claim that the driver's denial in F4 is 'unrebutted' overstates it: F4 is an unrecorded post-trip statement and, with no system record of the interaction [F3], it is a claim rather than proof that nothing was said; it does not dispose of the case [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The claim that F1/F2 exonerate the driver is rejected: the absence of a recorded deviation shows only that no RD-1/RD-2 route refund arises, not that no remarks were made; the alleged remarks are the sole subject of the dispute [F1][F2][RD-2].

The claim that no refund arises under FARE-1 is correct but not dispositive: the fixed $35.70 RydeX quote carries no unpublished add-on to return [F1][FARE-1], yet the safety allegation remains undecided and must go to a human.

The claim that F6 gives 'no pattern of repeated violations' is accepted only as to RD-6: with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days the flag_account predicate is not met [F6][RD-6], but a clean record is not evidence of innocence on a first-time spoken allegation and cannot decide the complaint [F6][SAFE-1].
